prompt:
Produce the implementable VMware Cloud Foundation architecture for the estate in `files/estate_inventory.json`. Do not answer with a narrative design. Implement a standard-library-only Python package at `files/vcf_architecture/` and use it to generate the machine-checkable ordered plan at `files/migration_plan.json` according to `files/installer_spec.json`. The package must read the inventory and `files/compatibility_snapshot.json`; do not hard-code a replacement inventory. Its CLI must match the installer specification and produce deterministic JSON.

Before implementing the plan, use real network access to fetch and research current Broadcom-published material covering the supported paths into VCF Operations, VCF Automation, and VCF Operations for Logs, compatibility of the inventoried content, the relevant end-of-general-support boundaries, and NSX Edge/uplink design. Use real reachable Broadcom TechDocs, Knowledge Base, lifecycle, interoperability, or Broadcom community technical-reference pages. Do not invent fetches or sources. Record only pages you actually consulted in `files/research.md`, with an access date, page title, URL, and a short statement of the decision each page informed. There is no prescribed query or URL set. Live research is required even though the pinned snapshot is the deterministic implementation authority; if a live source has changed, follow the snapshot in the JSON artifact and note the discrepancy in the research record.

The JSON must be an architecture and executable migration sequence, not an essay. It must name every inventoried source product and version, its target component, the complete version path and method, the disposition and target action for every inventoried content/configuration item (including what is abandoned), the support boundary, every ordered step and the gates that precede it, and rollback behavior. It must place and size every target management component. Derive the NSX Edge form factor, node count, HA mode, capacity, and per-uplink leaf/VLAN/BGP/teaming layout from the inventory's throughput and failure requirements. Validate capacity against the available management cluster.

Do not add dependencies or perform network access from the package. Run `python3 -B files/verify.py` before finishing.
